label: D2 after a repeated common a2->S2 transition (mid-episode, trials ~25-79)
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when the agent chose a2 and reached S2 through a common transition (never on a1, S1, or rare trials). It also needs the previous trial to have been a common a2->S2 trial as well (prev_action 2 with prev_common 1, or unknown at the window start): it almost never fires after a1 or after a rare transition. All predicate variables can be observed at D2. There is a strong episode-time dependence: the unit is nearly silent before trial ~20 and from trial 80 on, and its rate peaks at trials 40-79. Adding the window 25 <= ep_trial < 80 raises dev F1 from 0.67 to 0.83 (P 0.77, R 0.89, mass 0.90). Magnitude is larger when this trial D1 showed no reward (prev_reward 0: 28% of activations but 47% of mass), and it is higher in high-value steps. Silent on D1 and GO.

issues: All structural claims check out on dev. The unit is never active at D1 or GO (0 of 380619 steps each), never on action a1, state S1 or a rare transition (0 activations each). Only 103 of 56790 activations follow an a1 or rare previous trial. The base condition (D2 & a2 & S2 & prev not a1/rare) has R 0.998, P 0.508.
Reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.779, R 0.879, F1 0.826, MR 0.885. Dev is P 0.774, R 0.894, F1 0.830.

Mild overclaim on 'nearly silent before trial ~20'. The time dependence is a gradual ramp, not a gate. Within the structural condition precision is 0.135 at trials 0-4, 0.24 at 15-19, 0.33 at 20-24, 0.44 at 25-29 and 0.83 at 40-44, then falls from 0.86 at trial 74 to 0.48 at 79, 0.28 at 80 and 0.03 at 82. So the unit fires on about 20% of qualifying steps before trial 20, though only 6.7% of all activations happen there. The 25/80 cutoffs are a reasonable discretisation of a smooth ramp-up and a sharper ramp-down.

In 'repeated a2->S2', the condition prev_common != 0 also lets in the window's first trial (rel -3), where the previous trial is unknown. That subgroup's precision is lower (0.633 vs 0.831 for rel != -3) because the real, unseen previous trial was sometimes a1 or rare. This is a data artifact, not a flaw in the explanation, which already says 'or unknown at the window start'.

No systematic false-positive class remains. Precision is roughly flat across subgroups: prev_reward 0 0.71, prev_reward 1 0.80, good=S1 0.80, good=S2 0.77, value high/low 0.77/0.78. Long runs of rewarded a2->S2 trials have somewhat lower precision (0.72-0.78), and a rewarded trial right after an unrewarded one has higher precision (0.93). This shows up as decaying activation over long stable runs, but it is graded modulation, not a separable class. Adding value or the choice logit does not improve F1 (0.697 and 0.793).
The magnitude claim checks out: prev_reward 0 accounts for 28% of activations (16098 of 56790) and 46.6% of activation mass.
Missed activations (11.5% of mass on test) are mostly qualifying steps just outside the ep_trial window, plus small activations after an a2 rare trial. Nothing systematic.
No FUTURE variables are used. Every variable in the predicate is observable at D2.
